subject: [PATCH v4 5/7] sched/numa: scan PID-inactive VMAs for promotion

2026-09-30.patch_summary: This patch modifies the Linux kernel's NUMA (Non-Uniform Memory Access) memory management to bypass a filter that suppresses faults needed to promote hot slow-tier memory. The filter, which skips VMAs without recent PID activity, is disabled for promotion-only scans and only enabled when a VMA scan starts. This change allows for more efficient scanning of large VMAs and reduces the risk of starving in-progress placement scans. The patch also introduces a new field to track the last completed placement scan separately from other scans. With this modification, memory tiering can adapt to changing workloads and improve system performance.
